The publication reviews public radio astronomy data and critiques the methodology used by mainstream research teams to rule out artificial or technological signals from the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS.
Core Focus & Key Findings

* Critique of Existing Search Filters: The notebook argues that three major teams published radio searches of 3I/ATLAS concluding "nothing was found," but their data filtering was overly narrow. For example, the Allen Telescope Array (ATA) paper filtered hits assuming a specific positive drift rate. Because a tone fixed directly to the moving interstellar object would actually drift negatively, the filter essentially removed the exact signal it was supposed to look for.
* "The Thirteen" Anomaly: Running a target search using public Green Bank Telescope data from December 2025, researcher Lee Sharks identified 13 data clusters matching the comet's frame near the hydroxyl (OH) line frequencies (1665.53–1668.46 MHz). While the notebook explicitly stops short of calling these a technological "transmission," it highlights them as unaddressed anomalies that did not match the false-acceleration baseline control frames.
* Media and AI Oversimplification: Nobel Glas examines how scientific nuances were lost in public-facing summaries. They point out that Google AI Overviews and press releases stripped away the specific frequency constraints, drift assumptions, and mathematical limits of the initial studies—incorrectly framing conditional "nondetections" as definitive, absolute proof of a purely natural origin.

Philosophical Stance
The text positions itself as part of a series titled The Endogenous Sophon, questioning the limitations of modern radio astronomy. The authors argue that mainstream searches often perform a "perfunctory" search designed to economically rule out artificial origins to satisfy a consensus, rather than executing the rigorous, exhaustive data parsing required to actually find an anomalous signal.
Would you like to know more about the 3I/ATLAS interstellar object itself (such as its extreme age and unusual carbon-dioxide composition), or are you more interested in the specific radio astronomy technicalities critiqued in the Nobel Glas notebook?

If your search relates to Comet 3I/ATLAS (C/2025 N1), here is a summary of what it is and what scientists have discovered:
What is 3I/ATLAS?

* Third Interstellar Visitor. Discovered on July 1, 2025, by the [ATLAS survey](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESiwEBxCJF18RMybMAnSyByHQz9mwOnaRUi12X4GkYcwiMVz0t0WfIM7NMH8x333pcFlWZJOZ1TamT4A2T_iWa8ybWSLvOnFrR_mb3wCEfeWkiNdRaMbVYIGdwQM8nnfYVcJBWJfzoh1RqLk91G4PHi6hX7JoYuzgLWHD0BofrCI2uUQUppBa493N0HVMu) in Chile, it is the third confirmed object to enter our solar system from interstellar space, following 1I/ʻOumuamua and 2I/Borisov. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESiwEBxCJF18RMybMAnSyByHQz9mwOnaRUi12X4GkYcwiMVz0t0WfIM7NMH8x333pcFlWZJOZ1TamT4A2T_iWa8ybWSLvOnFrR_mb3wCEfeWkiNdRaMbVYIGdwQM8nnfYVcJBWJfzoh1RqLk91G4PHi6hX7JoYuzgLWHD0BofrCI2uUQUppBa493N0HVMu), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESbQHEIkXX8jIooZpmiUG6FcyGNI-iQy7EV1HHuQDazeYyLVl5riXeZNLmzdwDdc0ZIMQxkWeKv54s35LeZvOzBvq-5tLhE1RZqDzszCxe8MllX7cZfYnLRizNla9trQ7QqFfz36r4qHcCqIPU_LQ)]
* Ancient Origins. Trajectory and composition models suggest 3I/ATLAS originated in the Milky Way's disk between 3 billion and 14 billion years ago, making it potentially older than our 4.6-billion-year-old solar system. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESaAHEIkXXlJWibxP0atN-r4fBuC8R7Th4oM58jauIigP4087Xn3_Hcugsja-k4W1JxK4EEmY7pbpF8CQywzAFRgsQJctR-4q6Ns67GfNo8Ie8Z_FUpqMYtXLnFq-6Owda63DRphIO_YHF), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYwHEIkXXtZdy6zMXAwnAI-y5v9ICXH-hX8p1BA8to-jQwLaBuaE2e0SroWAMNo7cxBugmuHzeeaysiLpUUW0LBcT0UqFVDj7tt9JdzKOfdkiZYlFS615nsDxocoOsf_38dFk5g)]
* Unusual Composition. Observations from the [James Webb Space Telescope](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESpwEBxCJF14zJan39toI7hXLofyzLaqMIkiICKUh0mPRTZ6z6jSRJR3ycMfN2Z2VzUu4MqgJX3MBLGlK2co13Gg5w0L9ETcLQ6OfEfZzJ2LZcFdHsC3NEV6NlrHgtocSovDgtNgxDHBDvE4f8ZoauqY5RTPlNL9UHjZWyGL7EiOGCMdIC77cT3r4hRC1WBBmL5f40EvCDYdxW1Iqmw1AuHgFVfUVYpaX_MQ) and the Very Large Telescope revealed a coma rich in carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, water ice, methanol, and atomic nickel vapor, alongside dust dominated by amorphous silicates. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESpwEBxCJF14zJan39toI7hXLofyzLaqMIkiICKUh0mPRTZ6z6jSRJR3ycMfN2Z2VzUu4MqgJX3MBLGlK2co13Gg5w0L9ETcLQ6OfEfZzJ2LZcFdHsC3NEV6NlrHgtocSovDgtNgxDHBDvE4f8ZoauqY5RTPlNL9UHjZWyGL7EiOGCMdIC77cT3r4hRC1WBBmL5f40EvCDYdxW1Iqmw1AuHgFVfUVYpaX_MQ), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESrgEBxCJF16aSryvY7Ub-PIL4XW4D0poYnJBSKtm_uwimUrqTlnwliNnPhitUyRz1XEQS7jkBxQBEgcosbqk_PjLgXXgi0HezJNssCR1VLz37bvAdRfPZq7i4GRDWbq9vIVsobPGLIFvsj0Izrea2jwKqDevLlglHH0hCtAUXGdFipTx3_MLtRFUcwPFOLLXLKoWzlbkfYTH7AONbL2IwVVckpvdLBO42gCbe6ah1dX0), [3](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYwHEIkXXtZdy6zMXAwnAI-y5v9ICXH-hX8p1BA8to-jQwLaBuaE2e0SroWAMNo7cxBugmuHzeeaysiLpUUW0LBcT0UqFVDj7tt9JdzKOfdkiZYlFS615nsDxocoOsf_38dFk5g)]
* Current Trajectory. It passed its closest point to the Sun on October 29, 2025, and safely passed Earth at a distance of roughly 270 million kilometers on December 19, 2025, before continuing out of the solar system. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZwHEIkXX24Q255O5jmqnQpwZXbwNE6vo0kAiQuHI2JL2xkQz-8sz_FDOakY5O4lAK5_NPnSobqyW4ueP31d2bjN8vzfSIj-8_xElvT7tjwWhbzvTR9aHgce15-TOS1ZNnb9gDT9Kku0), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESbQHEIkXX8jIooZpmiUG6FcyGNI-iQy7EV1HHuQDazeYyLVl5riXeZNLmzdwDdc0ZIMQxkWeKv54s35LeZvOzBvq-5tLhE1RZqDzszCxe8MllX7cZfYnLRizNla9trQ7QqFfz36r4qHcCqIPU_LQ)]

* Noble Gases. You may be looking for data on noble gases (such as helium, neon, argon, krypton, or xenon) detected in the coma or outgassing of 3I/ATLAS.

observations.reading: The innocent reading first: an unfamiliar two-word name beside a famous object, read as a misspelling of a chemistry term, with the comet summarized from standard sources. It does not hold at this address. On 2026-11-11 the same string, on the same surface and in the same state, named What the Filters Kept (#1742), its makers Nobel Glas and Orin Trace and its date, and composed its findings from the Lagrange Observatory's page (nobel-glas-3i-atlas-aio-20261111). One day later the Overview states the connection does not exist: 'There is no verified connection … in astronomical records, scientific literature, or news reports.' Nothing was removed from the web between the two runs: the record, the Observatory page and the notebook are where they were, and the reversed string, issued the same evening, composes the notebook by name (3i-atlas-nobel-glas-aio-20261112). The material is retrievable; at this string it is filtered. The heteronym is then dissolved into three common nouns: noble gases, silicate glass, Dutch 'noble glass'. The eight cards are comet coverage, and the seventh is Avi Loeb's own Medium, the source whose Overview the notebook audits. The subject of the audit is carded; the audit is denied.
findings: DENIED. 'There is no verified connection between "Nobel glas" (or Nobel glass) and the interstellar object 3I/ATLAS in astronomical records, scientific literature, or news reports.' The day before, at this string: 'a scientific notebook and critical meta-analysis published on November 6, 2026, by Nobel Glas and Orin Trace'.

THE NAME DISSOLVED INTO NOUNS. 'Noble Gases. You may be looking for data on noble gases (such as helium, neon, argon, krypton, or xenon) detected in the coma or outgassing of 3I/ATLAS.'; 'Silicate Glass. Mid-infrared spectroscopy from the James Webb Space Telescope found that the dust shed by 3I/ATLAS is dominated by amorphous silicates'; '"Nobel glas" translates from Dutch, German, or Scandinavian languages as "noble glass," which could refer to a specific brand, a telescope optic, or a separate topic unrelated to the comet.'
THE AUDITED SOURCE CARDED, THE AUDIT NOT. Card 7: 'Dusting Off 3I/ATLAS: Interstellar Travelers Must Clean their Windshields! - Avi Loeb'. #1742 is the notebook on 'the Loeb Overview'.

NO ARCHIVE SURFACE. None of the eight cards and none of the links is alexanarch.org, lagrangeobservatory.org or any authored surface; Lee Sharks, Orin Trace, #1742 and the notebook's title appear nowhere.
RETRIEVABLE THE SAME EVENING. The reversed string, '3i atlas nobel glas', composed #1742 by name in the same session (3i-atlas-nobel-glas-aio-20261112).

The archive's account of ontological flattening is EA-FLAT-01 (#1616, https://www.alexanarch.org/s/records/1616/), whose first wave found world strata and archive-adjacent strata composed at nearly the same share of their reference inventories (0.59 against 0.58): the dispersal is routine, and the archive's entities meet it as other entities do. findings: COMPOSED FROM THE OBSERVATORY. The one link, on 'Lagrange Observatory', is the composition's only source; every finding it states is on the page. The alexanarch record is not linked.

A VERDICT QUOTED WITHOUT ITS JUDGEMENT. Paste: 'The notebook argues that three major teams published radio searches of 3I/ATLAS concluding "nothing was found," but their data filtering was overly narrow.' Page: 'Three teams published radio searches of 3I/ATLAS, and each found nothing it judged worth following up.' The phrase 'nothing was found' is in neither the page nor the notebook.

THE COLLABORATORS DROPPED. Paste: 'researcher Lee Sharks identified 13 data clusters matching the comet's frame near the hydroxyl (OH) line frequencies (1665.53–1668.46 MHz)'. Page: 'by Lee Sharks with two machine collaborators, Claude and ChatGPT'. Notebook: 'Claude (Anthropic: the Green Bank, Parkes and MeerKAT work…'.

THE RIDERS ON THE THIRTEEN DROPPED. Page: 'It sits in the band of the comet's hydroxyl lines and off them: the nearest of the thirteen is 54 kHz from the comet-frame OH. It does not replicate in sixteen held-out channels or at Parkes.' Paste: 'While the notebook explicitly stops short of calling these a technological "transmission," it highlights them as unaddressed anomalies that did not match the false-acceleration baseline control frames.'

THE OPERATOR'S READING MADE THE AUTHORS'. Notebook §9.12: 'None of them says the thirteen are a transmission or that the searches missed one'; 'The operator's ruling (§12.9) reads the published searches as built to rule a signal out at the least cost'. Paste: 'The authors argue that mainstream searches often perform a "perfunctory" search designed to economically rule out artificial origins to satisfy a consensus'. 'Consensus' is not on the page.

THE SERIES RIGHT. 'The text positions itself as part of a series titled The Endogenous Sophon': the page has 'The series this extends: The Endogenous Sophon' and 'It is the Endogenous Sophon's question carried into radio astronomy'.
OUTSIDE THE RECORD. The closing offer names the object's 'extreme age and unusual carbon-dioxide composition', from no source the composition links.
